text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state owned telecom monopolist has increased the price of a single impulse by one grosz to 0.18 zloty, the company said.
- Italy's Technipetrol firm will carry out complex modernisation of the fluidal catalytic cracking facility at the Plock refinery (PP) plant worth 50 million marks, PP said.
- Euro Agro Centrum (EAC) has decided to withdraw from a contract, which granted it a 51 percent stake in the Szamotuly -based oil-maker, EAC said.
- Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH) is planning to take over a controlling stake in the SBR Samopomoc Chlopska cooperative bank, BPH said.

- PZU insurance firm has strengthend its position as Poland's biggest insurance firm in 1996. However, its life subsidiary PZU Zycie gave way to competitors, a preliminary annual report of Poland's insurance industry said.

- The Dutch-based Gasunie gas distributor is planning to sell up to three billion cubic metres of gas in Poland as of 1997. Gasunie's director H. Verberg will conduct preliminary talks with the Polish government in February, company spokesman Ben Warner said.

- The board of the Warsaw-based Kredyt Bank has accepted the resignation of the former board member Jerzy Pron. He was replaced by Roberto Marzanti of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the bank said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Infor publishing has acquired a stake in the SW Nowa Europa publishing from the Italian-based Il-Sole-24. Infor now fully controls the Nowa Europa business daily, a recently signed contract said.
- OKI Poland computer peripheral maker's turnover was 30.5 million marks last year, which showed a 37 percent growth compared with 1995, OKI Poland director Piotr Nowak said.
- Poland will soon introduce duties on most grain imports, which were originally scheduled to remain duty free until end -June 1997, government spokesperson Aleksandra Jakubowska said.
- Poland's economy is likely to grow by 5.3 percent in 1997 after an estimated 5.8 percent growth last year, Nomura Economic Research said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Exbud construction firm has acquired a 73 percent stake in the Poznan-based PPBP construction firm worth seven million zlotys, Exbud said.
- Global Hotels Development (GHD) will soon start construction of six new hotels in Poland worth $250 million, GHD said.
- Fiat Auto Poland exported 600,000 cars to 38 countries, the company said.
ZYCIE
- Increasing obligatory reserves to 20 percent will significantly limit credits, which are the banks' main source of income, Creditanstalt Securities analyst Tomasz Bonecki -Duda said.
PARKIET
- The listed Novita carpet maker plans to earn a net profit of 6.1 million zlotys this year, Novita said.
- Kredyt Bank, GE Capital and Creditanstalt are intersted in the privatisation of the Polish Investment Bank (PBI) scheduled for the end of first quarter this year.
